searchText: It depends on whether the block is a worst case scenario block or a normalish block, or the simplest possible block. It also depends on what you mean by "handle", what system specs, over what period of time, with how much headroom, and which client. Ahh I was thinking if we increased gas limits where would it have to end 😂😂😂 Cause I see a lot of people saying they can go up 10x or more and the other side saying no we’re at the technical limit In my experience, the disagreement comes largely from two things: 1. Whether you care about CPU utilization, disk space, or network bandwidth. 2. What you believe the target hardware is for running an Ethereum client. Even using arbitrum gas is significant which is funny Based on the current aws/Ovh datacentres we’re using I guess my question would be what do people think the limit is. Obviously pools can always upgrade the specs of our current servers though they are already pretty good The people who say "we can 10x" usually only look at CPU utilization and consider the target hardware to be a modern server. The people who say "we are way past the limit" tend to be looking at disk space and consider an "off-the-shelf consumer laptop from retail store that is also used for other things" to be the target. Ah I see So 10x is feasible hahaha Only if you are in the first group. 🙂 I mean I expected L2’s to be much better The "right" way to do rollups is to do many of them. Having 1 or 2 rollups doesn't help scaling in any significant way. But looking at the breakdown on the gas price site you can see they are using up a considerable amount of space and after having used rollups gas still isn’t cheap What we want is for apps to have their own rollups. For example, Axie Infinity would run on an ORU or ZKR so their users would just do a one-time deposit when they start playing and then all of the game occurs over on the rollup. Makes total sense Unfortunately, everyone thought it would be a great idea to just have everyone on Ethereum pile onto one rollup together. Which doesn't help anything. Then ethereum serves as a central network between large corporations Yeah I doubt anyone expected nfts to takeoff the way they have 😂 While high gas is pushing people into expanding into rollups and L2’s many also seem to be taking the easy road to competitors so I guess there needs to be a balance Is there a chance to greatly reduce the software side burden of running a node/block producer? I heard turbo geth was making good headway but then became part of erigon? Yes. There are many efforts currently underway to try to reduce the operating costs of running an Ethereum client. Since storage is the biggest roadblock for regular users at the moment, state expiry, portal network, and some form of regenesis are the big ticket items. Ah ok ty Guessing everything is long term rather than short term though Appreciate the answers Yeah, the problems being solved are quite challenging and require a lot of research and development work. Also, many of the solutions are *way* harder since Ethereum is already launched and running. Things like state expiry would be pretty trivial if you were building a brand new blockchain. No surprise and not complaining since I know it’s a lot of work you need to be super careful about Aren't both Arbitrum and Optimism still rate limited? In other words, I think they're not running at (anywhere close to) max capacity for whatever hardware they are running their sequencer(s) on. I have a question about the economics, once we transition to PoS with validators and executors, the amount of ETH in the market will decrease because there is no reason to sell. The costs of managing a node is so little. Previously PoW, miners had to sell to exchanges so that they cam pay off their electricity. How will the ETH market function once it is hard to acquire ETH since no one is selling to exchanges. People will always be selling eth ~~to~~on exchanges, that's how speculative assets work At the very least there will be taxes to pay ^ people will want to buy it in order to pay transaction fees to use the network to do stuff which is why it's called a commodity asset, similar to how oil runs the US economy hopefully there will be more users than validators yes, it seems Micah and Chris are both unaware of this.. and maybe missing a bit of the forest for the trees. L2s are still early Yeah, many L2s have various kinds of training wheels on still (including upgradeability). https://l2beat.com/ provides a good overview imo (and there's https://l2fees.info/ as well) I mean if they are slower and have less capacity than intended I get that but currently they occupy quite a bit of space on the eth network and I assume that’ll only increase not decrease? Ah ok my mistake
